items.title: Section: The Four Demons Named and Defined

items.zh: 云何四魔？一、蘊魔，二、煩惱魔，三、死魔，四、天魔。蘊魔者，謂五取蘊。煩惱魔者，謂三界中一切煩惱。死魔者，謂彼彼有情，從彼彼有情眾，殀喪殞歿。天魔者，謂於勤修勝善品者，求欲超越蘊、煩惱、死三種魔時，有生欲界最上天子，得大自在，為作障礙，發起種種擾亂事業，是名天魔。
items.en: What are the four demons? The demon of the aggregates, the demon of affliction, the demon of death, and the demon of the deity. The demon of the aggregates is the five aggregates of grasping. The demon of affliction is every affliction throughout the three realms. The demon of death is beings of every kind, from every class of being, perishing, dying, passing away. The demon of the deity is: when one diligently cultivating excellent, wholesome states seeks to transcend the three demons of aggregates, affliction, and death, a being born as a deity of the highest rank in the desire realm, possessing great sovereign power, creates obstruction, generating all manner of disturbance — this is called the demon of the deity.

items.zh: 當知此中，若死所依；若能令死；若正是死；若於其死作障礙事，不令超越。依此四種建立四魔。謂依已生、已入現在五取蘊故，方有其死。由煩惱故，感當來生，生已便有殀喪殞歿。諸有情類命根盡滅、殀喪殞歿，是死自性。勤修善者，為超死故正加行時，彼天子魔得大自在，能為障礙。由障礙故，或於死法令不能出；或經多時，極大艱難，方能超越。又魔於彼或有暫時不得自在。謂世間道離欲異生，或在此間，或生於彼。或魔於彼得大自在。謂未離欲。

items.title: The Demon's Variable Power; Demonic Activity Opens

items.zh: 若未離欲，在魔手中隨欲所作。若世間道而離欲者，魔縛所縛，未脫魔罥，由必還來生此界故。云何魔事？謂諸所有能引出離善法欲生，耽著諸欲增上力故，尋還退捨。當知此即是為魔事。若正安住密護根門，於諸所有可愛色聲香味觸法，由執取相、執取隨好，心樂趣入。當知此即是為魔事。若正安住於食知量，於諸美味不平等食，由貪愛欲，心樂趣入。當知此即是為魔事。若正安住精勤修習初夜後夜覺寤瑜伽，於睡眠樂、於偃臥樂、於脇臥樂。由懈怠力，心樂趣入。當知此即是為魔事。
items.en: One not yet free of desire remains in the demon's hand, acted upon as it wishes. One who has become free of desire through the mundane path remains bound by the demon's bond, not yet released from the demon's snare, since one must inevitably return to be born in this realm again. What is demonic activity? Whatever wholesome aspiration towards renunciation has arisen being, through the power of renewed attachment to the sense-pleasures, soon abandoned and relinquished — know this to be demonic activity. When one who properly abides in closely guarding the sense-gates instead grasps at the general appearance and specific features of what is agreeable, the mind delighting to enter into it — know this to be demonic activity. When one who properly abides in moderate eating instead, through craving desire, delights to enter into unbalanced indulgence in fine food — know this to be demonic activity. When one who properly abides in diligently cultivating wakeful practice through the first and last watches of the night instead, through the force of laziness, delights to enter into the pleasure of sleep or lying down — know this to be demonic activity.

items.title: Section: Demonic Activity Closes — Topic Sixteen Complete

items.zh: 若正安住正知而住，於往來等諸事業時，若見幼少、盛年、美色諸母邑等，由不如理，執取相好，心樂趣入。或見世間諸妙好事，心樂趣入。或於多事多所作中，心樂趣入。或見在家及出家眾歡娛雜處，或見惡友共相雜住，便生隨喜，心樂趣入。當知一切皆是魔事。於佛法僧、苦集滅道、此世他世若生疑惑。當知一切皆是魔事。住阿練若、樹下、塚間、空閑靜室，若見廣大可怖畏事，驚恐毛竪；或見沙門婆羅門像、人非人像欻爾而來，不如正理勸捨白品、勸取黑品。當知一切皆是魔事。若於利養恭敬稱譽，心樂趣入；或於慳吝、廣大希欲、不知喜足、忿、恨、覆、惱及矯詐等沙門莊嚴所對治法，心樂趣入。當知一切皆是魔事。
items.en: When one who properly abides in clear awareness instead, through improper attention, grasps at the appealing features of what is seen and the mind delights to enter into it … know all of this to be demonic activity. Giving rise to doubt regarding the Buddha, the teaching, the community, the four noble truths, or this world and other worlds — know all of this to be demonic activity. Dwelling in a forest retreat, beneath a tree, near a charnel ground, or in a solitary quiet room, seeing something vast and terrifying, struck with fright, hair standing on end … urged, contrary to right principle, to abandon the wholesome and take up the unwholesome — know all of this to be demonic activity. Delighting to enter into gain, honour, and praise; or delighting to enter into stinginess, excessive craving, discontent, anger, resentment, concealment, malice, or deceit — the very states the renunciant's ornaments exist to counter — know all of this to be demonic activity.

items.title: Section: How the Four Demons Are Defeated — Topic Sixteen's Final Word

items.zh: 如是等類無量無邊諸魔事業，一切皆是四魔所作。隨其所應，當正了知。
items.en: All such countless, boundless demonic activities as these are entirely the work of the four demons. According to what is fitting in each case, one should correctly understand them.

items.title: Section: Setting Out Yet Arriving at No Fruit — the Seventeenth and Final Question

items.zh: 由三因緣，正修行者精勤發趣，空無有果。何等為三？一、由諸根未積集故。二、由教授不隨順故。三、由等持力微劣故。若有諸根猶未積集，雖復獲得隨順教授，強盛等持；精勤發趣，空無有果。若有諸根雖已積集，其等持力亦復強盛，而不獲得隨順教授；精勤發趣，空無有果。若有諸根雖已積集，亦復獲得隨順教授，而等持力若不強盛；精勤發趣，空無有果。若有諸根已得積集，教授隨順，等持強盛；精勤發趣，決定有果。如是名為由三因緣，空無有果；由三因緣，決定有果。
items.en: Through three causes, a genuinely correct and diligent practitioner sets out with full effort, yet arrives empty-handed, with no fruit at all. What are the three? First, because the faculties have not yet been accumulated. Second, because the instruction received does not conduce towards realisation. Third, because the power of concentration is too feeble. … If the faculties have already been accumulated, the instruction received conduces towards realisation, and the power of concentration is strong, then setting out with diligent effort, the fruit is certain. Thus it is said: through three causes, there is no fruit at all; through three causes, the fruit is certain.

blocks.text: The sixteenth and seventeenth questions: demonic forces, and why effort may bear no fruit. A short passage (0447c23) is untranslated. Fascicle 29 and the second yogic process end today.

"The demon of the aggregates is the five aggregates of grasping. The demon of affliction is the afflictions of the three realms. The demon of death is the death of beings. The demon of the deity is: when one cultivating wholesome states seeks to transcend the three realms, a god of the desire realm obstructs it." Venerable Miào Jìng: some beings do much merit but hold wrong views; their merit makes them powerful gods who obstruct others.
"One not yet free of desire remains in the demon's hand. One free of desire through the mundane path remains bound by the demon's bond." Only the supramundane path frees one.

Countless: failing to keep wakeful practice; grasping the appealing features of what is seen; in solitude "seeing something frightening"; doubting the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, the truths. "All such countless demonic activities are the work of the four demons."
Recognise them for what they are, and apply the antidote.

"Through three causes, a genuinely diligent practitioner sets out with full effort, yet arrives empty-handed": the faculties are not yet mature; the instruction does not conduce to realisation; the effort is not yet complete. Venerable Miào Jìng: "attaining concentration" means access concentration; "not yet mastered" means the root absorption not yet reached.

The second yogic process is complete: seventeen questions on practitioners, objects, instruction, training, failure, yoga, attention, the factors of awakening, the fruits, synonyms, Māra, and fruitless effort. Fascicle 30 opens the third yogic process.

quiz.q: What are the four demons, and why does Venerable Miào Jìng say the aggregates are a demon?
options: aggregates, affliction, death, deity; the body arises from affliction and in turn breeds affliction
quiz.why: "The demon of the aggregates, the demon of affliction, the demon of death, and the demon of the deity. The demon of the aggregates is the five aggregates of grasping." Venerable Miào Jìng: the aggregates are the karmic result that is our body; it arises from affliction and, once arisen, gives rise to affliction again — so it is a demon.

quiz.q: When does the deity-demon come to obstruct, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: only when one's diligence nears producing the path; before that the demon disdains to come
quiz.why: "The demon of the deity is: when one diligently cultivating excellent, wholesome states seeks to transcend the three demons of aggregates, affliction, and death." Master Cháng Bǎi: only when the practitioner's diligence reaches the point of producing the noble path does the deity-demon come; before that it looks down on them and does not bother to disturb.

quiz.q: Why does one detached by the worldly path remain "bound by the demon's bond"? What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: though desire is not active for now, the demon king's rope still binds him
quiz.why: "One who has become free of desire through the mundane path remains bound by the demon's bond, not yet released from the demon's snare, since one must inevitably return to be born in this realm again." Master Cháng Bǎi: though for now desire is not active, the demon king's rope still binds him.

quiz.q: Seeing something terrifying in a forest retreat is demonic activity. How does Master Cháng Bǎi say to handle it?
options: know it is false imagining and ignore it; contemplate emptiness, get up and walk, or open the eyes
quiz.why: "Dwelling in a forest retreat, beneath a tree, near a charnel ground, or in a solitary quiet room, seeing something vast and terrifying, struck with fright, hair standing on end." Master Cháng Bǎi: if this happens, know it is false imagining and pay it no heed — contemplate emptiness, get up and walk a little, or open your eyes, and it will dissolve.

quiz.q: Doubt about the Three Jewels is demonic activity. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say decides whether something is demonic or Buddha-work?
quiz.why: "Giving rise to doubt regarding the Buddha, the teaching, the community, the four noble truths, or this world and other worlds — know all of this to be demonic activity." Venerable Miào Jìng: whether it is demonic activity or the Buddha's work depends on your own single thought.

quiz.q: The third cause is "the power of concentration too feeble." The note, following the Pixunji, demands real absorption. What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng finds the Pixunji's standard too high, reading it as weak clarity and calm; Cháng Bǎi: access concentration still flawed and wisdom dull
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: attaining concentration means access concentration; "not yet fully mastered" means not having the four absorptions — this sets the bar very high. He also says: neither dull nor scattered — not scattered is calm, not dull is clarity. Master Cháng Bǎi: the access concentration attained is still full of flaws and wisdom is not sharp, so affliction cannot be cut.

quiz.q: When is "setting out with diligent effort" certain to bear fruit, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: accumulated faculties, fitting instruction, strong concentration — all three needed; missing any one, no fruit
quiz.why: "If the faculties have already been accumulated, the instruction received conduces towards realisation, and the power of concentration is strong, then setting out with diligent effort, the fruit is certain." Master Cháng Bǎi: lacking any one, the fruit of the path is not attained; only with all three causes complete is there fruit.
